beats.t: Square at noon. The scale was as big as a house.

The brass scale erected in the middle of the square had two plates each the size of a cart. Its majesty, shining in the sunlight, showed at a glance what the island of Jaeseong worships as a god. Not money, but scales. A god named Accuracy.
The noon bell rang. Twelve times. The moment the bell rang, the trial began. The air in the square was tense.
I'm shaking. But strangely, I don't want to run away. Those people are all watching. If they lose here today, those people will never be able to raise their heads.
That's right. Today's trial is not about a bakery, but the 'hope' of this island. So, we must win with evidence and win with our hearts. Either one alone is not enough.
The evidence is yours, the heart is mine. Same as always. Okay, ready to scream.
This time, it's not just about shouting, it's about being sincere. Shake the hearts of the people on this island with your voice.

Daejeoul was the court of the island of Jaeseong. There was no judge or lawyer. When each truth was placed on two plates, the scales weighed it and made a decision. On this island, the scale's decision was God's decision.

There was an old phrase engraved on the pillar of the scale. “What is priceless cannot be priced.” It is said to have been written a long time ago, before this island became obsessed with money. Now no one remembers what it means.

On one side was the Blue Rabbit contract, and on the other side was the evidence that Neo had collected overnight. Thirty-seven canceled order forms, insubstantial addresses of ordering companies, and a ledger at the top of the bait.

Yeon-i. This scale measures the ‘weight of truth.’ It is not only evidence, but also the audience's feeling that 'this is right'. So we have to win two things. Blue Rabbit's documents, and the resignation of the people of this island.
Resignation is probably the heaviest dance. Because everyone believes that ‘the Blue Rabbit will win anyway.’
So today, you only have to shake that belief once. 'Oh, you can win?' In that one moment, the entire scale swings towards us.
Island residents filled the square. People who had been fading to gray were raising their heads for the first time in a very long time.

On one side of the square stood the witnesses that Luna had called all night long. The noodle shop man, the blacksmith shop lady, and the regular at the morel bread. Everyone covered half of their faces in fear of the green rabbit, but their feet were here. That alone was great courage.
Did you see it, Yeon? I called them all! Everyone was closed at first, but when I told them about you, they came out! There are so many on our side!
Luna, you are truly the best guide today. Each and every one of those people is a real weight to put on the scale.
My sister stood quietly at the back of the witness stand. His face was still blurry, but just today he didn't run away and came out to watch my trial. Luna held his hand tightly.

The blue rabbit stood in front of the scale. For the first time, the slightest hint of tension flashed through his eyes as he looked around at the audience. This was the first time in his 30 years of business that he had seen so many people turn their heads to the plaza.
This one has a lot of audience. Well, that's good. Many people look at it. How truth weighs in front of the scales. And how that truth becomes lighter in the face of money.
Truth becomes lighter in the face of money? Let's see. Today it will be the opposite. I will prove to these people how light money is in front of the truth.
You are a very energetic customer. I am also very curious as to how long that spirit will last.
Go to the end! Our kite’s spirit is unlimited refills!
A small laugh escaped from the audience. At the mention of “unlimited refills,” the frozen air in the square loosened slightly. That one small smile was the first crack in today's trial.
A public trial, how romantic. great. Because the scale doesn't lie.

Our side first. The contract is here. Debtor's signature, seal, interest clause, collateral clause. Everything is fully equipped. You signed voluntarily and in very beautiful handwriting. There is no flaw anywhere.

The plate on the green rabbit side sat down heavily. A perfect document had weight in itself. A sigh came from the audience. “I guess that doesn’t work either… 」 The courage I had regained shrank again.

It's a perfect document. But do you know what the scariest thing in the world is? It's so perfect. A contract written by someone in a hurry usually has flaws here and there. Something this smooth gives the impression that it was made from scratch.
Hmm. You're sick. The scales don't tip based on your heart, sir.
Then let's go to physical evidence. It's my turn.
First, 35 out of 37 ordering companies do not have registered addresses. Second, the other two are all subsidiaries of Cheongtokki Financial Group. Thirdly.
Neo's voice was as straight as a knife. At the end of each sentence, the scales tilted a little in this direction.
The audience murmured. “You don’t have a registered address?” “So that means all those large orders were fake?” For the first time, instead of resignation, questions appeared in people’s eyes.

Fourth. The owner of the noodle restaurant and the owner of the blacksmith shop here suffered in the same way. Big orders came in, but disappeared when we got a loan. Same script, different actors. This is not a coincidence, it is repetition.

The noodle shop man raised his trembling hand. He was a person who could not even open his mouth for thirty years because he was afraid of green rabbits. “That’s right. So did I. Suddenly, orders for festival delivery started coming in at a rate of 100, but when I took out a loan, it stopped all of a sudden. I thought I was the only one who was unlucky... 」

As soon as one person opened his mouth, the dam burst. The blacksmith woman and the mill woman poured out the same story one after another. The injustice that each person had swallowed alone became a sound in the square for the first time.
The weight of those voices was placed on the scales. The scales have tipped noticeably in this direction. It was not the evidence, but the weight of the voices recovered.
Look, Neo. Because one person has the courage, everyone follows suit. They say fear is contagious, but courage is also contagious. Right now in this square, the container infection is spreading.
You were right. The scales are falling. Now, one last shot.
Third, appraise the ink on the day of the contract. Gold line.
As the platinum-colored thread ran over the contract, other words oozed out from underneath the beautiful letters. It was a signature on a blank piece of paper that was stamped first.

Gold wire reads the order in which ink dries. The ink that dried later will bleed out on top, and the ink that dried first will bleed out on the bottom. Now, look. The ink on the signature dried before the ink on the article. That means—

Signature first, clauses later. This is physical evidence that the debtor did not sign after reading the clause, but rather received his signature on a blank piece of paper and filled it in later. It's a clear deception.
The blue rabbit's ears trembled. His contract, which no one had touched for thirty years, was being stripped bare by a single platinum thread.

Ink emotion. Customer, where did you get such technology? It’s an appraisal method that doesn’t exist in this era.
Let's call it
statistics. As always.
Look, Neo sometimes imitates my speaking style. It's called 'statistics'.
The signature came first and the clause came later. It was a blank contract.

The truth revealed by Geumseon loomed large over the square. For everyone to see. What the baker's sister signed was a blank piece of paper, and Blue Rabbit later filled in the terms on it. The collateral, interest, and recovery of the image were all lies attached to the signature.

The audience was very excited. “I signed a blank piece of paper too!” “So are all our contracts fake?” Each person recalled their own contract. It was a moment when one truth became the truth of the entire square.
You heard it, everyone! Get your signature on a blank paper and fill in the terms later! This is Cheong Rabbit’s real sales secret! This is how everyone’s contracts are made!

The scales have tipped very, very heavily in this direction. Physical evidence and public opinion were put on the table at once. The Blue Rabbit's plate floated into the air. As far as the decision, it was truly a span.
This can't be happening. This can't be happening. Thirty years. In thirty years, this scale has never once betrayed me.
The scale did not betray me. The scales were originally on the side of truth, but you have been deceiving them for thirty years. Today, for the first time, the scale actually measured the weight.

Blue Rabbit's hand went into the cloak. The composure from just a moment ago disappeared, and the gaze of a cornered animal took its place. He was about to bring up something, something he really didn't want to write about.

My sister covered her mouth with both hands. From blurry eyes, clear tears flowed for the first time in a long time. It was the moment when my own injustice was proven to the world for the first time.
The square was in turmoil. The scales have tipped heavily in this direction. The angle was broken for the first time in Blue Rabbit's smile.
Customer. Are you now denying my entire 30 years of business?
Denial of thirty years of fraud, to be exact.
Someone in the audience shouted, “That’s right!” Then, “That’s right!” and “That’s right!” erupted from all over the place. Voices that have been suppressed for thirty years filled the square today.
Can you hear me, CEO? This is the weight of public opinion. It’s not just documents that are measured on the scale. Those voices, they all have weight.

The blue rabbit did not answer. But at that moment, something old flashed in his eyes. Thirty years ago, the face of a young rabbit whose voice was heard by no one. He tried hard to ignore the fact that the voices that filled the square were what he had wanted so much back then.
That's right! You've been doing bad things for thirty years! Scales, weigh this guy very heavily!

Laughter erupted from the audience. The sound of laughter rang out for the first time in the square that had been oppressed by fear. Laughter mocking the blue rabbit. The weight of that laughter was placed on the scales again.

Blue Rabbit's perfect smile was distorted for the first time. My ears were tilted back, and my fingertips were trembling slightly. In thirty years, no one on this island has ever laughed at him. How dare you laugh at those who set prices.
Don't laugh. Even laughter can be priceless. Everyone, that laugh you just saw is very expensive. You will receive it back via invoice later. Every single person.

But it was already too late. Once laughter broke out, it spread faster than fear. The injustice that had been suppressed for thirty years filled the square in the form of laughter. The scales were decidedly tilted in this direction.

Did you see it, sister? People laugh. In the square where everyone held their breath for fear of the green rabbit. This is a real victory that came before the invalidity decision. People can smile again.
The decision was right before our eyes. The two letters ‘Void’ were about to land on the scale.

The square held its breath. The scale, which had not tilted even once in thirty years, was about to tip over to the other side of the blue rabbit for the first time. In the eyes of the gray people, a long-forgotten light returned. The light called hope.
won! Yeon, we won! Look at the scale, scale! Fully towards us—

My sister put her hands together. For the first time in a long time, a human-like anticipation spread across his blurred face. Maybe we can get it back. The face, the name, and an ordinary morning with my sister who was like a daughter to me.
Look, sister. There are some things that cannot be priced. The scale just proved that. My sister's injustice was heavier than the blue rabbit documents.

It was that moment. At that moment when victory seemed within reach, the Blue Rabbit laughed very quietly. It was not the laughter of someone who lost, but the laugh of someone who saved their last hand.
At that time, the blue rabbit stopped laughing. Then he took something out of his cloak pocket.
It was an old pocket watch. A black case that looks like it was carved out of the night sky, not gold or silver. There was a thread engraved on the lid.
The moment Neo saw the clock, Neo's entire body stiffened. The ends of his mane stood on end. That watch, that black case, that piece of thread — he knew. Like a very old nightmare.
That thread pattern. It's her stuff. The fact that Blue Rabbit has this means that the exploitation of this island was her hand from the beginning.
That woman? Neo, do you know that watch? Is it related to the ‘Chairman’ on the blue rabbit?
I'll explain later. Now, we have to snatch the watch before that lid opens. If that opens, this trial will no longer be a trial. The rules of this world themselves are being rewritten.
The audience was frozen. People who had regained their courage just now began to bow their heads again to that single black clock. My instinct knew. That thing is above the scale.
Yeoni! That watch is scary! It's the exact opposite of how the water was shining earlier. That… It smells like something is being erased!
Luna is right. I don't think I should open that. Neo, stop it now!
I really didn't want to write this. It is something given to you from above, so if you take it out carelessly, you will be scolded.
Yesterday I asked where I got that watch. I didn't answer. I won't pass today. Don't open that lid. That's not something you can afford.

You had that same face yesterday too. I really like that face. It's a face that recognizes something scary. Oh, can you handle it? It's not up to me to handle it. I am a person who only opens the lid.
Before Neo could move, the blue rabbit's thumb opened the lid.
Click. Something that was not time flowed from the clock. Dark blue fog, the smell of ink, and the crunching sound of an invisible pen scratching paper.
Fraudulent contract. It's time to rewrite, customers.
The contract on the scale fluttered alone. A new clause slowly grew over the blank signature that was evidence of invalidity. The ink was drying against time.
“All observers of this trial guarantee with their breath that they will not raise objections to the decision.”
What is this? The letters are being written arbitrarily!
Black hands grew out of the shadows of the square. The gray residents lowered their heads without a scream. The scales began to tilt crazily in the opposite direction.

The first thing to be erased were the mouths that had laughed earlier. “No objection” was engraved in the mouth of the noodle shop man, and “End of hearing” was engraved in gold in the eyes of the woman at the blacksmith shop. The first item on the bill that Blue Rabbit predicted was that smile. The voice that was recovered was once again sealed in a single clause.
My sister stumbled. The tears that had been clear until just now began to blur again. The proven injustice was being erased before my eyes.
Sister! No, your face is blurred again! Yeon proved it all! The scale was on our side! Why, why are you doing this again?

Luna tried to run to her sister. However, the words “No access to officials” were engraved on the child’s feet. My feet were stuck to the floor. My sister was being erased right before my eyes, and I couldn't take a single step closer.
This is too much. This is really too much. What did we do so wrong? I just wanted to bake bread, deliver bread, and live together.

Yeon-i saw the scene with blurred eyes. Luna's feet are tied, her older sister is erased. This injustice, this helplessness, was very similar to certain nights in the world where he originally lived. No matter how hard I tried, those nights seemed to slip away and get ruined.
This is fate? How can someone who worked hard be erased like this? no. This isn't fate, it's just something someone wrote like that with a pen. If you wrote it, you can rewrite it. certainly.
too. It wasn't possible. Beating the Blue Rabbit on this island was impossible from the beginning. For no reason, even you…
Sister! Don't say that! It's not over yet! The scale just tipped completely over to us! That's a foul, not a loss!
But golden letters were about to be engraved in Yeon's voice. “Plaintiff’s remarks are subject to review by creditors.” Before the words came out of my mouth, the clause tried to swallow them.
Even my words. Are you saying I can't even talk anymore?
Unnecessary remarks cost money, sir. Because I really hate costs. Now, would you like to quietly go through the disposal process?

Yeon tried to open her mouth. However, the words “Plaintiff’s remarks are over” tried to seal my lips. The voice dispersed like fog. The sense of becoming an item. The feeling of one's name being changed to a single line in a contract.
Stop, Yeon. Stop now. I really can't see you all being erased because of me. My face, just... I'll give up. Just you, just you, run away.
Just then, a voice burst from Yeon-i's mouth as she was about to be sealed. It was the last word before the clause was swallowed.
I won't give up! Your face is yours! It's not a line written in that blue rabbit ledger, it's the face that smiled at Luna every morning! You can never erase that, not even with a scale or a pen!

That cry rang out in the square. Jo Jo tried to cover up those words, but his sincere words lasted a little longer than the ink. Some of the audience members, who had turned gray, raised their heads for a moment at those words.
It's noisy. I told you that the longer you talk, the more interest you get. great. Then, I'll put that mouth on the disposal list as well. All together, down.
single gold.
Platinum's slash cut through the black fog. However, the ink continued from the cut spot again as if laughing. No matter how much they were cut, the provisions were constantly rewritten.
Gold line! Ten ways!

Neo stretched out ten strands of platinum thread at the same time. I tried to tie all ten areas of the fog together. However, in an instant, the words “Creditors’ Assets” were engraved on all ten strands. The thread began to entangle its owner.
My technology binds me. This isn't about having a strong opponent, it's about taking control of the rules of the world. You can't win head on. From the front—

Neo's mane gradually turned gray. The platinum color of the watchman who had been forging for a hundred years was covered in each and every clause. He gritted his teeth and held on, but even that was just a sentence before the pen that rewrote the world.
Neo! Your mane! Stop it, you too will be erased!

That's the root. Reflection comes from breathing, not from hands. If you rewrite it with haste, it will be swallowed up like before, but if you rewrite it with even breath, no false seal can overcome it. Okay, that's it. I read in the afternoon.
When day came, Baekmun brought an armful of contaminated books and piled them on the reading table. It was a practical textbook that Yeon needed to revive.
'This person isn't lazy, he's tired.' 'This kid wasn't bad, he was lonely.' … 'This person didn't fail, he just had bad luck.'

Each time Yeon read the original text one by one, the black seals faded and the real sentences that had been pressed came back to life. Five or ten books a day. Yeon’s reading speed got faster every day.

Good! Reading has become a habit now. What remains is the third threshold, rewriting. Reading and rewriting are different. Reading is revealing someone else's sentence, and rewriting is engraving that sentence back into the world. Rewriting requires your breath.
Take root!

Yeoni's turquoise vines burrowed under the black emblem. This time, he did not stop at 'reading and revealing' the original text, but instead held onto the sentence and pushed out the entire black seal to re-engrave it into the world. It was the first success of rewriting.
rewriting is now possible! And without hesitation! Now that I can breathe, I can't get swallowed up like before. The roots of a tree not only pierce the soil, but they also pierce lies. again!
done! I wasn't scared this time! Since I can't breathe, the black letters can't be transferred to me! This is rewriting!

Day two, day three. Yeon’s reflection deepened every day. At first, it took half a day to read one book, but later, one black shelf was recovered in one day. As the books that were suffering regained their light one by one, Yeon-i's blue-green color also deepened.
Then one day, Yeon came across an unusually heavy book. The book that has been on the shelf the longest, with seven layers of black seal. Even the White Gate had not been touched for a long time.

This book has too many stamps. It's been pressed seven times, so I can't even tell with my fingertips what the original text is underneath. No matter how hard I try to read it, it keeps slipping away.
That's the most deeply sick book on this shelf. A stamp that has been pressed for a long time sinks the original text to the bottom. Don't overdo it. That's only after you fill up the last pillar—
No. I want to try it now. I think some people slip because they are scared. Third principle, don't be swayed. I can do that now. Breathe evenly and slowly.

Yeon closed her eyes and took a deep breath. Inhale and say, ‘I am unwavering.’ Exhale and say, ‘Below here is the real thing.’ I gave up my impatience and very slowly slid my fingertips under the seven layers of seal. One layer, two layers, three layers...

caught. At the very bottom, very small. 'I still wanted to live.' … Even though this person collapsed seven times, at the bottom he still had the desire to live. Even under seven layers of debt, it didn’t go out.
I pierced through seven layers. You caught the bottom line. A book I haven't been able to read for a hundred years.
I will rewrite that feeling of wanting to live. Take root!

Yeoni's turquoise vines pushed up the seven layers of seals one by one. “Incompetent,” “bankrupt,” “insolvent”… The black letters broke one after another, and “I Still Wanted to Live” rose in gold from the bottom. The book that had been suffering for the longest time finally took a deep breath.
done. This person is no longer a ‘wasted person’ but a ‘person who wanted to live’. A person who does not die even if it collapses seven times. thank god. I'm so glad.

Yeon-i. You have surpassed me now. I couldn't get through this book for a hundred years, but you did it in a few days. In your retelling, there is something I don't have. A heart that hurts at someone else's bottom as if it were your own. That's what makes you stronger than me.
No. It was because Baekmoon taught me. If I were alone, I would have just gotten scared and run away from this book. Thank you, Baekmoon. I will rise above and use this power properly.

In her spare time as a trainee, Yeon became quite fond of library life. The lantern fish now recognized Yeon-i and sat on her shoulders, and Baek-moon experimented with new dishes at every meal. But suddenly, Yeon really missed the things she had left behind.

Ah, I suddenly want to eat triangle kimbap. Spicy tuna. And that ordinary dinner in front of the convenience store refrigerator, wondering ‘what to eat today.’ At the time, I didn't know it was so precious.
I don't know what triangle gimbap is. Missing something means having a place to return to. It's good. I am… I don't even know where the place I miss is.
Neo, do you have nowhere to go? So where are you going when this is all over?
Well. I haven't even thought about it that far. My mission is to send you home. After that... Well, I'll go and think about it then.

Then come to my house. I'll buy you triangle kimbap. Oh, since you are a lion, you have to eat the big ones, so about ten. And there is also a bakery that my sister runs. Croissants are really delicious. Neo, it's a bit funny to imagine you eating a croissant.
The lion eats a croissant. I can't draw a picture. but… Not bad. That kind of future too.

Yeon said those words with a smile, but those words stayed with Neo for a long time. A place to return to. The future of eating triangle gimbap together. It was a picture that a watchman who had to pay for stealing time should not dare to draw. But on this night, Neo also imagined that picture for a moment.
Well, then, if I want to go eat that croissant, I have to finish this training quickly! Baekmoon, did I do my part today? Samgak Gimbap is calling me!

Heh heh. I don't know what triangular kimbap is, but if that's what drives you, it's good. Okay, enough for today. When you smile like this, this old library lights up. There hasn't been this much noise in a hundred years.

Then Baekmoon, you should smile more often. Now, let me tell you one of my world’s buzzwords. This is what you shout out when you're having a hard time. ‘Oh, I don’t know, I don’t know! 'Let it happen!'
‘Let everything happen’? For a librarian, that's very... It's an unholy spell. To the old man who worked hard for a hundred years to 'make' all the documents in the world.
Ah, so we need more! You carried it all on your own for a hundred years. Sometimes, you can say ‘I don’t know, I don’t know’ and relax your shoulders. Now, follow along. Oh, I don't know!

Heh heh. Oh, I don’t know, I don’t know. hmm. It's a spell that makes your shoulders feel a little lighter than you think. For the first time in a hundred years, I learned that there are things it is okay to let go. You not only teach fortune telling, but you also teach old people how to live.
Baekmoon, you must not abuse that order. If the library's dirty shelves are left unattended, Yeon becomes a mountain of things to write about.
Oh, that's right. Baekmun, don’t use ‘I don’t know, I don’t know’ to polluted bookshelf. Because that’s my food line!

The three laughed again. The library, which had been silent for a hundred years, was filled with laughter in these few days. Baekmun felt that this commotion was more precious than any document he had kept all those years. So, I was a little afraid of sending these kids up.
Above there was a pocket watch, a blue rabbit, and something even scarier waiting. I hope this laughter will not die out even in the darkness. Baekmun quietly prayed like that.
Baekmun's classes were harsh yet kind. Breathing in the morning, reading during the day, writing at night.
First, a fraudulent contract cannot overcome the original. No matter how thick the copy is, one line of the original text will collapse it.

Second, the rabbit's watch only adds sentences and cannot erase them. Even if it looks like it has been erased, the original meaning lives underneath. So the key to fighting is not cutting, but rereading.
Is there a third child? For some reason, I think there are up to three.

That's clever. Third is the most important. Third, that clock feeds on the opponent's 'wavering' and increases its strength. If you are afraid, read that fear and add 'you lose' to your sentences. So you should never waver in front of the clock. As long as you don't shake, the clock can't do anything to you.
So, you had them answer ‘Why do we fight?’ in the reading room. In order not to be shaken, I have to be firm about why I am here. Because people who have answers won't be shaken.

That's right. Okay, let's sort it out. One, the original beats the copy. Second, a clock can only be written over and cannot be erased. Third, if it is not shaken, the watch is powerless. If you don't forget these three, you will definitely win. Now, let’s learn it with our bodies. rewrite again

For the actual battle, Baekmun created an illusion that imitated the ticking of a pocket watch. When the clock rang, Yeon-i's breathing became shallow for a moment. The helplessness of the court was about to be revived.
It's shaking! Don’t be defeated by that sound! Remember your breathing! 'Why am I here!'
'To protect the names around me with my writing!' … it's okay. I'm not afraid of the sound. Even if it ticks, my breath doesn’t waver!

When Yeoni memorized the sentence she had engraved in the reading room, her breathing, which had become shallow, became deep and even again. No matter how the illusion of a pocket watch ticked, Yeon's turquoise color did not waver. The third principle is learned firsthand.
Okay. very good. I don't get shaken by that sound anymore. Even if you see a real clock above, you are ready now. All that remains is the perfection of the rewriting. Now, keep going.

While the training continued, the library's contaminated shelves became noticeably brighter. As the number of books that Yeon-i brought back to life exceeded one hundred or two hundred, an entire section of the shelves that was once pitch black regained its light. What Baekmun could not do on his own for a hundred years, Yeoni was able to do in just a few days.

That's amazing. This area is a place I haven't touched in over fifty years. You brought it all back to life in just a few days. If this continues, the day will come when, thanks to you, this library will have no black shelves for the first time in a hundred years.

That's great then! After reviving everything, we all have tea together with Baekmun under the light of the new lantern. Ah, but I’m not really going to buy it and get a job like this, am I? Baekmun’s assistant, Yeon-i.

Heh heh. You are welcome anytime. But don’t you have a home to return to? Rather than being this old man's assistant, you should live your life in your own world. Still, with just those words, a hundred years of loneliness melt away.

Yeoni looked happily at the bookshelf where the revived books were shining side by side. Each of those books was someone's recovered truth. Yeon-i was proud that this power could save so many people. As I rise above, I promise to use this power to save more people.

You really have a talent for saving others. In Jaeseong, I read other people’s values, and here, I bring back other people’s truth. I'm glad you have this power in your hands. What would the world have become if it had been in the hands of a bad person?

That's right. This power is scary. It can save others, but if used incorrectly, it can also label others as 'incompetent'. Blue Rabbit is writing it exactly like that. So, I will make sure to use this power correctly. Just to save it.
Take root!
This time, Yeoni's vine took root not on the floor, but on the crest. Roots dug under the overwritten black letters and pulled up the original sentence.

The black overwritten letters were pushed out, and the real letters pressed underneath them resurfaced in gold. The contract that Cheong Rabbit forged began to regain its original meaning in front of Yeon-i's roots.
Okay. The roots of a tree not only pierce the soil, but they also pierce lies. again!
Baekmoon, I feel like your hands are no longer mine. The brush sticks perfectly to my hand and doesn't fall off.
Heh heh. It is a state of becoming one with the brush. It's a great prize.
No, that's not true, it's because the food has dried up and doesn't really fall off.
Hmm. Just wash it.
Oh, you just seriously said 'the state of becoming one with the brush'. Baekmoon is also quite a fool.

It was not an illusion, it was the teacher's hope that the student's hand would truly become one with the brush. Now, stop laughing. There's still half left to copy tonight. When you’ve finished washing the brush, sit back down.
Yes. (Baekmoon, you're kind, but you give me a lot of homework...)

Every night, Yeon-i struggled with the written homework Baek-moon assigned. It was a training exercise to transcribe the world's unfair sentences by hand and engrave those feelings into your fingertips. Even though her wrists went numb and her eyes closed, Yeon didn't stop. Because each and every stroke of this will give me the strength to get my sister back.
z

Yeon's transcription skills improved day by day. The writing, which was crooked at first, has now become neat enough to be placed side by side with the white text. More than anything, my heart began to fall into the writing. Even though the same sentence was written, warmth oozed from what Yeoni wrote.

Huh. Did you write this manuscript? The writing smells like a person. This isn't done with technology. It means that you put your heart into each and every sentence. You really are a natural at this job.

It's just that the owner of these sentences keeps coming to mind. I hope that these wronged people will find some comfort when they look at their sentences again someday. As I thought and wrote like that, my sincerity naturally came into my writing.

That's the final secret of rewriting. Not technique, but sincerity. A feeling of caring for other people’s sentences as if they were one’s own. You already have it. All that's left is to not waver in front of that clock.

While Yeoni was learning rewriting, Neo also trained alone by her side. In the backyard of the library, in a dark yard where even lantern fish don't come often. A golden thread was pulled out from between the silver mane, splitting the air without a sound. The gold wire is thinner, and the gold wire is deeper.

Yeon used to look through the window while doing her homework. Neo's swordsmanship was beautiful, but somehow sad. Rather than cutting something, it felt like I was swinging the knife to withstand something.
Baekmun made a strange face every time he saw Neo's breath. The long-lived fox's eyes did not miss the scent of time hidden by the silver sentinel.
How is it that the more you break your fast, the more lonely it becomes? What on earth have you been forging for so long to cut? It seems like the point of the knife is pointed towards you.
When it comes to cutting, to cut.

Huh. Your answer is very blunt. But the old fox is not fooled. The sword you sharpen is not for cutting anyone. It's a sword that I inevitably sharpen for moments I wish would never come. When that moment comes, you'll be the one who hurts the most.

Baekmun, you really read too much. you're right. The day this knife is used will be the day I lose the thing I least want to lose. So please, I hope that day never comes. I pray for just that every day.
The secret of a person who has sharpened such a sword for a long time is naturally so lonely. warden. I have one question. Is that the child you are trying so hard to protect?
Yes. Sending that child home safely. That's my only reason. It doesn't matter what happens to me after that.

'It doesn't matter what happens after that.' Watchman, save your words. Because you already have someone by your side who will be sad without you. Do you know that that child is sad that he never really saw your face?
How did you know that?

Heh heh. That's the way that kid looked back at you when he came out of the reading room. Okay, this is the end of the old man’s meddling. Just keep this one thing in mind. Protecting it is important, but being with it after protecting it is more difficult and more precious.

Neo didn't answer. He just put away his golden sword and stood in the dark yard for a long time. Baekmun’s words were the first to crack a small crack in my long-forged resolve. To be with you even after that. That was a future that Neo had never dared to see.
On the fourth day, Baekmun stopped the two people together in the yard. This time, it was a practice we did together, not separately.

Guys, if you go up there, you won't be fighting alone. You must learn how Yeon’s wood and the watchman’s iron fit together. Wood is cut by iron, but iron loses direction without wood. The five elements play against each other, but they also save each other.
Me and Neo practicing fighting together? But Baekmun, I heard that wood can be cut by iron. So Neo won't beat me?

If you just look at it, it is. But take a good look. When the watchman's iron opens the way, your tree spreads its roots along the way and catches the enemy. The watchman cuts down, and you hold back. The iron breaks down the door, and the wood pulls out the truth inside. Separately it's half, together it's complete.

Baekmun erected a scarecrow covered in black seals in the air. Neo's gold wire flew first, cutting down the seals and scattering them, and Yeoni's turquoise vines dug into the cracks and pulled up the original text. For the first time, metal and wood moved as one.
done! Neo split the black seal, so I uploaded the original text underneath it! We're perfect partners!
We are in sync. Your roots came right through the gap I cut. Not bad. No, quite… I feel reassured.

Good! That's it. Watchman, don't try to cut them all down on your own. Because that child can read the ‘seal of the heart’ that you cannot cut. And Yeon, the watchman opens the ‘hard shell’ that you cannot break through. Let's believe in each other's better half.
Neo, let's decide on a name for our duo. hmm… ‘Iron Tree Club’? Or ‘Kummok combo’? Oh, how about ‘The Watchman and the Flower Pig’?
That last one is a no-no. It sounds like the title of an old children's book.
Huh? Is that good? ‘The Watchman and the Flower Pig’. It's an absolute bestseller. Baekmun, please put a copy of this in the library!

Heh heh. That's good. If this story ends well, I will write it myself and put it in the best place in this library. 「The Watchman and the Flower Pig」. So make sure to come up with a good ending. If you want to live up to the title.

Yeoni and Neo looked at each other and smiled. A few days of training had turned the two from simple companions into true comrades in arms. The iron became the direction of the tree, and the tree became the reason for the iron. The two were working together as one towards the final fight that would take place above.

But the longer the training went on, the more nervousness grew in a corner of Yeon's mind. If the time in the library and the time above flowed at the same speed, Luna and her sister would have been waiting for her for several days by now.
Baekmun. While I've been training here for several days, how much time has passed up there? Luna and my sister, didn't something happen while I was waiting?

Don't worry. Time passes more slowly in Inseong’s library than on Jaeseong’s island. A few days here is just a day up there. While you gain strength here, time above awaits you. This is the only gift this library has given you.

Thank goodness. Still, I don't want to take too long. Before my sister's face becomes more blurred, before Luna becomes more lonely. Now I can rewrite, I am not shaken by the sound of the clock, and I have regained my sense of self. At this level, isn’t it time to slowly move up?
I think so too. Yeon is ready. The last remaining pillar, Shinmi, is in the rabbit safe anyway, so you have to retrieve it from above. There is no reason to delay any longer.

Yes. You guys are right. I've taught you almost everything I need to teach you now. All that's left is the actual battle. but… Before you go up, there is one thing I must tell you. There is a very old story related to the Librarian's signature on this wrist.
Oh, that's it. I asked you a few days ago, but you said 'I'll tell you tomorrow' and kept putting it off. Are you listening now?

Yes. If you go up, you'll come across it in the Blue Rabbit Vault. … I'll just correct one thing. I won't tell the story. The story that I have swallowed for a hundred years is constantly refined to make it easier for me to hear. Tomorrow I won't tell you, you will read.
Yeon nodded. The old pain in Baekmun's voice made me guess what kind of story would unfold tomorrow. The last night at the library was approaching.
Baekmun left for a moment and returned carrying an old wooden box. Inside was a brush that looked very old. It was an unusual brush with a soft bluish-green color on the handle.

I'm giving this to you. When I was a wandering librarian, it was the brush with which I rewrote the world's unfair sentences. It’s called ‘main writing.’ It is a brush that only writes the original meaning and cannot write lies. … And the last thing I wrote with this brush is the half of it that I haven't been able to read for a hundred years. If it were you, this brush would wake up again.
You're giving me something so precious? It's Baekmun's. Can I take this?

The person who uses the brush is the owner. It has been asleep in my hands for a hundred years, but in your hands, it will write the truth of the world again. Take it. This brush will help you when rewriting the original contract in the Blue Rabbit Vault. It is the first and last gift that the old librarian gives to his student.

When Yeon held the pen in her hand, the bluish-green color returned to the tip of the brush that had been dormant for a hundred years. The brush recognized its owner. Yeon’s hand and brush fit perfectly, as if she had been waiting for a long time.

I woke up. Light returned to the tip of the brush. Baekmoon, I will definitely use this carefully. And when it's all over, I'll get Baekmun's librarian's signature back and return it to you along with this brush. So that Baekmoon can rewrite the world's unfair sentences again.

Heh heh. When that time comes, the two of us will sit side by side and rewrite the world's unfair sentences. With your brush and mine. With that one picture, this old man can survive for another hundred years.
You are a good teacher and a good student. Yeon, take good care of that brush. Because it is a weapon and an item that contains Baekmun’s hundred years of history.
Yes! Can I try it out? Here, on this blank piece of paper… I'll write any lie. 'Yeon is a coward.'

When Yeon-i tried to write a false sentence with her pen, the tip of the brush slipped before it even touched the paper, and the letters were not written. On the contrary, when I wrote ‘Yeoni never gives up until the end,’ the brush went out smoothly and glowed gold.
It's true! No lies are written, only the truth is written! This brush is a completely honest brush. It would suit me well. I really can't lie either.

Heh heh. The brush and the owner are similar. Yes, that brush only writes the original meaning. So, even in the face of Blue Rabbit's false contract, the brush will not waver and will only rewrite the original. Your honesty and the honesty of your brush have met - there is nothing to be afraid of now.
Thank you, Baekmun. I will protect this brush like my life. And with this, I will rewrite everything about you, Luna, and Baekmoon. With a real name and a real face.

Yeoni held Bonpil tightly to her chest. A brush filled with a hundred years of writing, and the seven stars that one has regained. Now we were almost ready to go upstairs. All that was left was the old story of Baekmun and the final battle.
Late at night after training, Yeon went to see Neo, who was left alone in the yard. After the daytime joint training, there was one thing I wanted to ask.

Neo. Aren't you sleeping? You know. I saw myself in the mirror in the reading room during the day, and she said that. I've never seen your face properly. He said he always looked at his back. Because you are always standing in front of me.
face.

Yes. So, I'm going to take a good look at your face right now. Just stay still. Hmm, your eyes look like this. I always thought it was scary, but when I looked closer, it was really... Those are kind eyes. Why didn't I know this?

Neo awkwardly tried to look away, but held back. Yeon’s eyes were carefully reading her face. Those eyes that read the deepest thoughts of others were now resting on Neo's face. The watchman felt like showing his face to someone for the first time in a hundred years.
Why are you looking at me like that? It will wear out.

It doesn't wear out. And now I know. The reason you always showed your back was because you were standing in front to protect me. But Neo, now I sometimes stand next to you. Then I can go with you while seeing your face. I don't like following people with their backs turned to me anymore.
Stand next to
. That makes it more difficult for me to protect you.

It's okay. Because now I will do the same to protect it. You saw it during the day. You cut me down, I hold you down. He said we were mates. Partners should stand side by side, not in front or behind.

Neo was silent for a while. Then, very slowly, he took a step towards Yeon and stood next to him. Not in front, but side by side. That one small step melted just a little something in the sentinel that had been frozen for over a hundred years.
This is the next level.
Yes. Just right. Thanks, Neo. For standing side by side.

The two looked up side by side at the night sky with lantern fish flowing in silence for a while. It was a night that needed no words. Yeon suddenly felt that the most reassuring thing in this unfamiliar world was the warmth of the seat next to her.

When I returned to my room and finished copying, I trembled ever so slightly every time my pen touched the paper. It seemed as if the brush was trying to draw another letter that Yeon had memorized for a long time, rather than the letter she was trying to write. Yeon put down her brush and asked what had been on her mind.
Baekmun. What is that golden letter on your wrist, your signature? Is that why you can't go out?
Baekmun’s pen paused for a moment on the ink bottle.

I am a librarian. This is the seal the library places on its librarian. If you receive this, you won't be able to take a single step outside the library. It's been like that for a hundred years. What did I entrust and receive this... It would be better to have a brush say that instead of my mouth.
Yes. But Baekmun. You don’t have to force it. If it hurts, you don’t have to take it out. I just feel bad that Baekmoon has been holding it alone for so long.

No. Now is the time to take it out. If you go up, you will encounter the final piece of the story in the Blue Rabbit Vault. Now is the time to pass on the story that has been swallowed up for a hundred years to you. However, not today. Today is a day for you to sleep well.

Bai Wen put down the pen with dry ink and looked at the lantern fish outside the window for a long time. A hundred years were reflected in those eyes. Yeon didn't ask any more questions, but just poured a cup of warm tea into Baekmun's teacup. It was comfort instead of words.

I'll listen carefully to tomorrow's story. And Baekmun. At the end of the story, whatever it is that hurt Baekmoon, I will rise above and take it back. The Librarian and the person Baekmoon was trying to protect.

Instead of answering, Baekmun smiled comfortably for the first time in a very long time. For the first time in a hundred years, I can share this old story with someone, not just myself. The last few days at the library were coming to an end.

That night, Yeoni fell asleep with the regained warmth of Imo in her heart. Seven stars glowed softly in my heart. If you fill in the last one, you have a complete constellation. Tomorrow we will hear the old wounds of Baekmun, and soon, we will rise again. To my sister, to Luna, and to the last pillar.

The pen that Baekmoon had given was placed at the bedside, emitting a subtle turquoise light. The brush, the star, and the determination quietly kept the sleeping Yeon-i. Learning at the library was almost over, and the real test was waiting up there.
Episode 22 · Fourth Pillar — The End. Continuing from Episode 23, “The Fish That Doesn’t Run Away.”

beats.t: It was the morning of the promised day. But this time, Yeon went first before Baekmun called.

The area where contaminated bookshelves suffer the most. Baekmun was already sitting there in an old chair. With the heavy attitude of someone who is about to tell a story that has not been told to anyone for a hundred years.
Baekmun. Today is that “tomorrow.” You promised yesterday. Instead of talking, he said he would borrow my paintbrush.
… It was like that. But after thinking about it all night, I thought it wouldn't work either. Today it's just this old man speaking out loud. There's no reason for you to see it yourself.
You said yesterday that if Baekmoon speaks out loud, it will be refined to make it easier for you to hear. That's what Baekmoon said.
… Heh heh. My words are holding me back from my student. Yeon. This is a story that needs to be refined. If you don't polish it, the listener will get hurt.
Instead of answering, Yeoni took out the pen from her pocket and held it with both hands. The bluish green color of the tip of the brush quietly awakened.
Baekmun. I'm not afraid of getting hurt. I'm more scared that Baekmoon got hurt alone for a hundred years. You don’t have to talk about it. I'll read it.

Baekmun hesitated for a long time, then pulled out the torn and scorched half from deep within the robe with trembling hands. It was a contract that had not been read in its entirety for a hundred years, with marks where it had been folded and unfolded once.
… Then I will warn you in advance. There is no story in this half. The whole day is included. If you take root, you will go there, not what you read.
I know. So I'll go to the roots. You can run away if you see it with your eyes, but you can't run away from the roots. … Take root!
A blue-green root spread out from the tip of the pen and dug into the burnt spot of the charred half. The ash crumbled, and the sentence beneath it breathed for the first time.
But the sentence didn't come to mind. Instead — I held on to Yeon-i. Not on the paper, but inside the paper, something grabbed Yeon’s wrist.
Huh? Baekmun, this is not being read... Get sucked in! My hands won't fall off!
Hold on! Don’t let go of your pen! As long as that brush holds your name, you can definitely come back!
Yeoni! … Baekmun, I can’t go in. There's no name on that piece of paper. I'll hold on to it here. A place for that child to come out.
The entire library made a very loud sound of turning a page. And Yeon-i stood in the middle of the night a hundred years ago.
first page. The library had a stronger smell of ink than it does now. There wasn't a single book on the shelves yet, and the ceiling seemed much lower. Inseong’s library from a hundred years ago.

White light poured down the stairs like a waterfall. It was a sight where the sincerity that the blue rabbit had poured down for a hundred years finally flowed back up. The black hands touched the light and dispersed without a scream.
What is that! Light comes up from the stairs! The black hands are afraid!
This energy. It is the energy of the Great Book. Could it be that Baekmun... Crossing the threshold? Without a librarian?

It was impossible. Baekmun, who lost his librarian, said he could not even take a step outside the library. I was trapped inside that threshold for a hundred years. But now, the white light was clearly coming towards this safe. Something had called him.

My contract. The contract signed with Baekmoon with his paw stamp. 'This library will always be on your side'... That fair contract is what brought Baekmoon here! A promise made with sincerity is stronger than the threshold!

A white fox landed on the library with the sound of pages turning. Lantern fish followed the hem of the robe like stars. The old librarian, who had been trapped inside the threshold for a hundred years, finally came out.
Sorry I'm late. It's been a hundred years since I stepped outside the threshold, so it took me a long time to find my shoes.
Baekmun?! How did you get outside?! You said you couldn’t come out without a librarian’s signature!

You stamped the front paw, right? A legitimate contract becomes a temporary pass for the librarian. ‘This library will always be on your side’ — that sentence is what brought me here. A sentence with a clear meaning is more powerful than a threshold.
Are you coming out for the first time in a hundred years for me? Taking that risk without a librarian?
The disciple is in danger, so the master can't just be brushing books on the threshold. Besides, I too am a hundred years behind on what I should receive from that thief. It just worked out well.

Baekmun looked around at the three people who were covered in wounds. Yeon has claw marks on her back, Neo is bleeding, and Luna is exhausted. For the first time in a hundred years, something hot filled the old librarian's eyes. These kids even broke into the Blue Rabbit safe for themselves.

You're hurt a lot. This old man says he will retrieve one of his librarians and find one of his wishes. You guys, to this extent. Saying thank you is not enough. So don't pay me back. From now on, I will use my last strength to write this great book.
Baekmun. I couldn't climb this mountain range by myself. My knees buckled. But since Baekmoon came... I think it will work now. I think just the two of us could retake this entire mountain range.

Of course. Your brush and my hundred years come together. Two people can lift weights that cannot be lifted alone. That's the principle of humanity. Come on, Yeon. Give me your hand. I will share my roots with your brush.

Baek-moon placed his hand on Yeon-i's original pen. The old librarian's 100 years of history flowed into the blue-green color, and his original pen shone dazzlingly. It was a moment when the power of the teacher and the sincerity of the student merged into one.
It's warm. Baekmun, a hundred years are flowing into my brush. I'm not scared anymore. Because you are not alone. If you're with Baekmoon, you can rewrite anything.

Baekmun rolled up the sleeves of his robe. The golden handcuffs “Librarian Retrieval Complete” were still wrapped around my wrist. A librarian without a librarian sign. I can't use my full strength. But those eyes were those of the ambassador who wandered the world a hundred years ago. And next to him, there was a disciple who was trying to get the perfect star back.
One hundred sentences. What does that old fox think? A half-assed topic without a librarian's signature!

It's been a hundred years. I still remember the face on which you faithfully earned my trust for half a year. That face took my Somang away. From that day on, I waited for a hundred years to see this face again.
Hope? Ah, that girl. Taken as collateral a hundred years ago. Are you still holding on to that? It's so foolish. All that time because of a worthless child.

Yeah, it wasn't even worth it. By your scale. But that child was my everything. The value of ‘everything’ that you will never understand. Today, I will teach you how terrible that price is. Forged for a hundred years.

It's been a while, thief customer. A hundred years worth of late fees, get it all today. Half of it? okay. I am half. But that child is intact. And if half me and that whole child are combined — one fraudster like you is enough.

When Baekmun raised his staff, the lantern fish scattered throughout the stand, illuminating the darkness. The blue rabbit's hunting lights were replaced by the light of the library. The black hands touched the light and shrank. After a hundred years, the light of the Great Book invaded the Blue Rabbit's vault.
Baekmun is here! Neo, Luna! Now there are four of us! Baekmun, I can do everything I learned to rewrite! Let’s win together!
Yes! You rewrite the original. I will tie that thief's watch. The sentinel represents the front, the water child represents pollution. Now, pay off your hundred-year-old debt today!

When Baekmun swung his staff, lantern fish surrounded the blue rabbit's pocket watch. The ticking clock stopped momentarily as it was enveloped in the light of the library. The clock that had been rewriting other people's fate for a hundred years lost its power for the first time.

Your watch, it's been a while. The watch that stole my signature a hundred years ago. Today I will tie you up. Although there is no librarian, a hundred years' worth of resentment from this library's lantern fish is gathered here!
Oh no! The clock isn't moving! That lantern fish took my pocket watch—!

Lantern fish 'like'. Do you know what those fish are? The unquenched sincerity of the documents you dropped here after weighing them down for a hundred years has turned into a fish. The hearts you trampled on have come together and are now tying your watch. This is justice, you thief.
That's ridiculous! Things that have no value! The trash I discarded! How dare you break my watch!

It's not that the value isn't there, it's just that you didn't recognize it. There is no worthless sincerity in this world. Since you haven't known that for a hundred years, today your hands will be tied by those sincerity. Yeon! The clock has stopped! Now is your chance!

The blue rabbit's pocket watch stopped ticking as it was surrounded by a school of lantern fish. The clock that had been rewriting the fate of the world for a hundred years was caught by the sincerity it had trampled on. The blue rabbit, which had lost its ability to write, now only had claws.
Now! Baekmoon tied his watch! If the clock stops, the blue rabbit can't rewrite it! Now I'm not alone in rewriting the original! Baekmoon, let’s do it together!

Yes! Now, let's reuse these mountains! I'll hold the watch and hand out the roots, so you can read the sentences! The power of this old man who has been with these documents for a hundred years will be put into your writing brush!

With the joining of the White Moon, the tilted scales became balanced again. Now it was the blue rabbit who was cornered. Its polite smile completely peeled off, and the hunger underneath revealed its claws. But this time, there was a hundred-year librarian behind the three.

Blue Rabbit. Earlier, I couldn't climb this mountain range by myself. But it's different now. With Baekmoon, Neo, and Luna. There are four of us. And the sincerity of all these mountains is on our side. Now, for real. I will take this library back from you.
Even without a watch, I still have claws! Jaeseong’s claws have been forged for a hundred years! That kind of brush trick, bringing pieces of paper back to life—!

I block those claws. While Yeon retraces the mountain range, your claws can't get past me one step. Luna, you will stay by Yeon’s side. Stop pollution with your water. Let Yeon fully focus on rewriting.
Yes! I will protect Yeon! Even though I used up all the water, I had to squeeze out every last drop! Yeon, don’t worry, just use it! Save all the people of these mountains!

Good formation. The sentinel blocks the way, the water child guards the side, and Yeon and I trace the mountain range. Come on, Blue Rabbit. The sincerity you have trampled on for a hundred years will all be revived today. And that's the end of your empire.

Yeon raised her pencil high. The tip of the brush containing the hundred years of the hundred letters shined dazzlingly. After that, Neo blocked his claws and Luna collected the last of the water. The four became one and launched a final counterattack toward the heart of Jaeseong. It was a moment when the empire of value was about to collapse before the will.
Episode 25 · Jaeseong’s Claws — The End. Continued from Episode 26, “All the Pillars in Their Place.”
